chunks: Pour upon us Your rain, Your blessing, Your sustenance and Your mercy,
And give us a drink that is beneficial, quenching, and producing herbage,
With which You cause to grow what has been lost, and revive what has died,
Beneficial for freshness, abundant in yield,
With which You water the dry plains, and make flow the valleys,
And cause the trees to leaf out, and lower the prices,
Surely, You are Powerful over whatever You will.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific benefits of rain requested in this Shia supplication?
ai.summary: This supplication, often cited in Shia devotional literature as a model for rain prayers (Du'a al-Masith), emphasizes the holistic nature of divine sustenance by linking meteorological phenomena to economic stability and agricultural revival. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing rain not merely as a physical necessity but as a manifestation of Allah's mercy that restores both the material landscape and the socio-economic well-being of the community. The invocation concludes with the attribute of Divine Power, reinforcing the theological belief that all natural cycles are subject to God's will.

en.sayed-ali-raza: do pour on us Thy mercy, Thy blessing, Thy sustenance and Thy pity,
and make us enjoy a drink which benefits us, quenches our thirst, produces green herbage
with which all that was lost gets a growing and all that had withered comes to life again.
It should bring about the benefit of freshness and plentifulness of ripe fruits.
With it plains may be watered, rivers may begin flowing,
plants may pick up foliage and prices may come down.
Surely, Thou art powerful over whatever Thou willest.
